svg.title: An agent buys one API call: discovery, x402 exact payment, ERC-8004 feedback
svg.desc: Sequence diagram: An agent buys one API call: discovery, x402 exact payment, ERC-8004 feedback. 9 participants: Client agent, Bazaar discovery endpoint, ERC-8004 Identity Registry, IPFS or HTTPS host, Seller resource server, x402 facilitator, Token contract (EVM chain), ERC-8004 Reputation Registry, and Indexer or reader. 14 steps, 13 crossing a trust boundary, 13 failure branches. Based on several protocols x402 v2.0 ERC-8004 Draft (text of 2026-01-25) (2026-01-25). Step 1: Client agent to Bazaar discovery endpoint: GET /discovery/resources (Bazaar). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The listing is stale and the server now asks for more: The live 402 response wins the client must compare it with its budget again. Step 2: Client agent to ERC-8004 Identity Registry: Read tokenURI and getAgentWallet (ERC-8004). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The agent NFT was transferred: agentWallet was cleared on transfer getAgentWallet returns no wallet until the new owner binds one again. Step 3: Client agent to IPFS or HTTPS host: Fetch the registration file. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The file is gone or does not list the endpoint: Nothing on chain flags it the client should not pay that endpoint. Step 4: Client agent to Seller resource server: GET /weather (no payment header). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 5: Seller resource server to Client agent: 402 Payment Required with PAYMENT-REQUIRED. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 6: Client agent to Client agent: Check payTo against agentWallet, sign EIP-3009. If payTo differs from the agent's agentWallet: Neither protocol forces this check a client that skips it can pay an address the agent never verified. If The amount is above the spend cap: The SDK rejects the entry and no payment is created. Step 7: Client agent to Seller resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The header is malformed: The server answers 400 (invalid payment). Step 8: Seller resource server to x402 facilitator: POST /verify, run the handler. This step crosses a trust boundary. If isValid is false (for example insufficient_funds or invalid_exact_evm_payload_signature): The server answers 402 again and the handler does not run. If The handler fails: The server does not settle, so the client is not charged. Step 9: Seller resource server to x402 facilitator: POST /settle. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The settle call times out or returns settlement_pending: Indeterminate: on settlement_pending the server retries settle once and the facilitator reconciles against the hash it broadcast after a timeout with no hash, the server can check the authorization nonce on chain. The reference middleware sends no data unless settle succeeds. Step 10: x402 facilitator to Token contract (EVM chain): transferWithAuthorization (facilitator pays gas). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The nonce was used or the balance dropped: The transaction reverts and the facilitator returns success false. Step 11: Seller resource server to Client agent: 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 12: Client agent to IPFS or HTTPS host: Publish the feedback file with proofOfPayment. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 13: Client agent to ERC-8004 Reputation Registry: giveFeedback(agentId, value, valueDecimals, tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI, feedbackHash). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The caller owns or operates the agent: Reverts with Self-feedback not allowed. If valueDecimals is above 18: Reverts with too many decimals. Step 14: Indexer or reader to IPFS or HTTPS host: Fetch the file, check hash and txHash. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The txHash does not exist or pays someone else: Nothing on chain flags it and getSummary still counts the value only off-chain scoring can discount it.
